briefing.text: News buzz is led again by Information Technology (87.4, +0.4 on the day, -0.5 on the week; NVDA, MSFT, AMD, AVGO, CRWV). Financials fell most on News, buzz -5.9 (-6.2 on the week) with mentions up 15% and sentiment 0.02 (BAC, UBS, MS, GS, C). On X, Healthcare buzz rose 15.9 to 51.0 on mentions up 200% (STLN, APMD, LTGO), and Consumer Staples edged up 0.7 to 88.6 with mentions up 26% (TGT, HIMS, WMT, COST). On Reddit, Energy rose 3.4 to 86.2 (BP, NOV, GEV, CVX) and Real Estate rose 1.5, while IT mentions fell 24% (NVDA, ANT, AMD).

TTWO #1: 102 articles in 2 days (61 positive, 3 negative); the top headlines are about GTA 6 skipping discs (GameStop CEO) and a stray Fastly item, so the news fits the GTA VI launch theme.
TGT #2: 48 articles, mostly positive; headlines say the stock heads for its best year since 2019 on a Q3 turnaround, which supports the rank.
COPPER #4: only 2 articles, both on Druckenmiller being short copper; thin news, so it does not explain the rank.
DJI #5: 8 articles, mixed; headlines cover DIA fund buying and futures ahead of a listing, with no clear driver for the move up.
DIS #6: 46 articles (29 positive); Disney, Target and ASO hit 52-week highs and Netflix guidance is in the mix, which fits the price move.
HOUSING #7: 1 article on the NAHB index showing nearly half of builders cutting prices; light coverage.
INTU #8: 18 articles, mostly negative or neutral (stock below its 50-day average); earnings are due today, which is the likelier reason for the rank.
NVDA #9: 1,359 articles (448 positive, 177 negative); Moody's confirmed its Aa1 rating and chip stocks rose premarket, though the price is down after earnings.

TTWO ranks first mainly on attention: Reddit, X and News mentions are about 1.5 times its own normal, with X at 1.45, plus volume 1.29 above normal and a 1.9-sigma price move (+6.2% in 24h). Its catalyst is the GTA VI launch markets on Kalshi and Polymarket. TGT is second, up from 6, on the strongest attention (1.93 overall, 2.01 on X) and volume 1.35, with a +4.0% move; open interest is below its normal and a KPI market resolves soon. IPC is third, up from 47, driven mostly by a large 3.3-sigma price move and attention 1.24, while its volume is low (0.22), so it rests on the move rather than on money flow.

notes: Ranks are by the scoring of record (pick_rank, w2). Prices and moves as of the last pull of the day. Facts from public data; not investment advice.
